an.tip.depth10: At 10-15 BB most hands should be all-in or fold. Avoid raising and folding, and avoid calling.
an.tip.depth25: At 25-40 BB re-shoving all-in over an open is often the best play. Calling and playing after the flop with this stack loses for you.

an.tip.positionBTN: The button should be your best seat. Fewer calls, more raises, and keep betting when checked to.

lp.title: How luck is calculated
lp.allin: An all-in here means: all the chips are in the middle, cards are still to come, and nobody can act any more. From that moment the result depends only on the cards that are dealt, so it is a clean measure of luck.
lp.equity: Equity: your share of the pot if this exact situation were played out over and over. It is not estimated: the app goes through every possible remaining board (up to 1,712,304 of them preflop) with the real cards of everyone involved. Ties split the pot, and side pots are handled.
lp.ev: Expected (EV): equity × pot, minus what you put in. What you win on average in this spot.
lp.luck: Luck = actual − expected. Positive: you won more than the cards deserved. Negative: less.
lp.badge: The dashboard sums the luck of every all-in in the period and compares it with how much that luck could swing by chance: an all-in with 50% equity for a big pot swings a lot, one with 95% equity hardly at all. The result is the number of "typical swings" your luck is away from zero.
lp.levels: Very lucky: +1.5 or more · Lucky: +0.5 to +1.5 · Average: between −0.5 and +0.5 · Bad run: −0.5 to −1.5 · Worst run: −1.5 or less. Two lost coinflips are "Average"; losing a series of 80% all-ins is a bad run. With fewer than 20 all-ins the badge says the sample is small.
lp.bb: Everything is counted in big blinds, so an all-in at 25/50 weighs the same as the same all-in at 500/1,000. Under the badge the app says how rare your result is for a player with average luck, e.g. "a run this bad or worse happens to about 1 in 6 players" (from the normal distribution: −1 typical swing or worse is about 16%).
lp.moment: Luck always uses the equity at the moment of the all-in. The replayer also shows how the equity changes as the flop, turn and river come, but those numbers are only for watching; they do not change your luck.
lp.example: You have {aa} against {kk}, 100 BB each, all-in before the flop. Your equity is about 81%.
lp.exampleMath: Expected = 0.81 × 200 − 100 = +62 BB. If you win: actual +100 BB, luck +38 BB. If you lose: actual −100 BB, luck −162 BB.
lp.reading: Good decisions show up as a positive expected number: you get your chips in as the favourite. Luck swings up and down and tends towards zero over many tournaments. The orange line on the dashboard is your result with that luck removed.
lp.limits: Limits: measured in chips and big blinds, not dollars (no payout structures needed). Only all-ins where every player's cards are known count, as in PokerTracker. A "bad beat" is losing with 80%+ equity, a "suckout" winning with 20% or less.

In a bounty tournament the summary gives only the total you received and the hand histories hold no bounty payouts, so whether you reached the paid places is not in the files: bounty tournaments are left out of ITM (their money still counts in profit and ROI). def.vpip: VPIP: how often you put chips in voluntarily preflop (call, bet or raise; completing the small blind counts, checking the big blind does not). Out of hands with a preflop decision (no walks, no all-ins forced by the blind).
def.pfr: PFR: how often you raise preflop (any raise, a limp-raise too). Same hands as VPIP.
def.rfi: RFI (raise first in): how often you open with a raise when everyone before you folded (no limpers). Chance: your first decision in an unopened pot, not in the big blind.
def.threebet: 3-bet: how often you re-raise when exactly one raise came before your first decision (callers allowed, so a squeeze counts). An all-in you cannot raise over (a call would put you all-in) is not a chance; an all-in for less than you have is (isolation).
def.fold3: Fold to 3-bet: how often you fold when your open (not all-in) is re-raised once.
def.shove: Open shove: how often you open all-in when everyone before you folded. Out of the RFI chances at this stack.
def.ev100: bb/100 by EV: the result per 100 hands without all-in luck (in a hand with an all-in the EV counts, not the result).
def.shoveCell: Open shove at {band}: {count} of {n} RFI chances at this stack

dp.intro: Your play by stack at the start of the hand (in big blinds). Open shove is counted out of the RFI chances in each band, so every band has its own base (n).

trend.note: The arrow compares the last 30 days with the rest of your history and appears only for a change beyond noise (|z| ≥ 2.5, 500+ hands and 100+ chances on each side), at most one at a time. Now: {state}

lp.sd: Analysis → Overview splits the result in BB into hands you took to showdown and the rest: without showdown (uncalled shoves included). An uncalled shove wins the blinds without showing cards, so it is a steal, not a showdown; a called preflop all-in always shows cards and is a showdown. The dashed line is the total by all-in EV: the gap to the total is the all-in luck described above.
an.roiTip: ROI with tickets at face value on both sides. No interval here, to keep the tile readable: the 95 % interval (how far your long-run ROI may be from this number, given how many tournaments you played) is in Money, next to the verdicts.

The verdicts "beyond chance" come from it: a group is called winning or losing only when the whole interval is above or below zero. The ROI tile in Analysis leaves the interval out to stay readable and links to Money instead.

help.title: Help
help.start.title: Getting started
help.start.body:
The app reads two kinds of files from PokerCraft (GGPoker): hand histories and tournament summaries, as .txt or .zip (a PDF with a text layer works too). PokerCraft lets you download about ten tournaments at a time, and hand histories only from the last 90 days, so import after every session.

In Import choose the folder with the files: a preview lists the tournaments, untick any you do not want, then import. With "Watch this folder" new exports come in on their own while the app is open. Importing the same files again changes nothing; "Re-read every file" rebuilds everything from the files (only needed after an update).

Left out, with the reason shown: cash games, Sit & Go, PLO, tournaments in other currencies, freerolls and promotions ($0 buy-in), and summaries the app does not recognise (a safety catch for a change in GG's format). Tournaments you ignore yourself can be brought back in Settings.
help.dashboard.title: Dashboard
help.dashboard.body:
At the top, your last session: tournaments that ran with gaps under three hours. "Session details" opens its screen: luck in all-ins, the session against your usual play, busts, bad beats and the biggest pots to review.

Below, a period: the last session, 24 hours, 7, 14 or 30 days, or under "More" 3 or 6 months, all history and your own dates. Four tiles: profit (tickets at face value, the cash part under it), ROI, tournaments and luck. One chart switches between profit in $ and the result in BB with and without all-in luck. "Worth knowing" names the best tournament, the tickets won and whether your play changed beyond noise.
help.tournaments.title: Tournaments
help.tournaments.body:
The list filters by period, buy-in, format and entry (from the start or late). A tournament page shows the place, prize, cost and ROI, every entry with its level and starting stack, and a warning when the files show fewer entries than the summary.

The stack chart switches between big blinds and chips (a deep run can grow in chips while it falls in BB). Every all-in is a dot: green won, red lost, grey split; its tooltip shows the cards, your equity and the luck. A click opens the hand.

Multi-day events: every day-1 flight that went through joins its Day 2 as one tournament (the cost of all flights, one final place). When PokerCraft offers the Day 2 hands but no summary, the event counts what is known and is flagged; pokertracker provisional <id> <amount> counts a prize you type in until the summary comes and replaces it.
help.hands.title: Hands and the replayer
help.hands.body:
Hands finds hands by period, buy-in, format, position, starting hands (click or drag across the grid), stack in BB, preflop action, all-in, showdown and result (actual or by EV). The preflop actions are the Analysis definitions, so "3-bet" finds exactly the hands Analysis counts.

A click opens the replayer: step through the hand, play it, see the equity at each all-in. Under it, the previous and next result of your search. "Copy the hand" gives a text for forums: positions instead of opponents' names, stacks in BB, every street, the result.
help.analysis.title: Analysis
help.analysis.body:
Every rate is counted over its own chances, as PokerTracker 4 does, with n (the number of chances) under it; under 30 chances it is greyed.

  • VPIP: you put chips in voluntarily preflop (call, bet, raise; completing the small blind counts, checking the big blind does not). Out of hands with a preflop decision: no walks, no all-in forced by the blind.
  • PFR: you raise preflop (a limp-raise counts).
  • RFI: you raise when everyone before you folded (no limpers); never in the big blind.
  • Open shove: that raise is all-in; counted out of the RFI chances at the same stack.
  • 3-bet: exactly one raise came before your first decision (a squeeze counts), and you re-raise. An all-in you cannot raise over is not a chance; one for less than you have is (isolation).
  • Fold to 3-bet: your open (not all-in) was re-raised once and you fold.
  • bb/100 by EV: the result per 100 hands with the all-in EV in place of the result.

The trend compares the last 30 days with the rest of your history (500+ hands and 100+ chances on each side) and shows an arrow only beyond noise (|z| ≥ 2.5), one at a time.

Leaks and strengths test every spot by EV against a baseline (a call from the blinds against folding) and correct for all of them together: a card appears only at q ≤ 0.05. The closest spots are listed apart, still within chance. The starting-hand grid shows each hand by EV against folding it; grey under 30 hands. The showdown lines split your result into hands that reached showdown and the rest.
help.money.title: Money
help.money.body:
ROI counts tickets at face value on both sides: a satellite returns the seat's value, a tournament entered with a ticket costs its full buy-in, so the total matches the cash that moved; "cash part" leaves tickets out. Next to each ROI, a 95 % interval (a bootstrap over your tournaments): where your long-run ROI probably lies. A group is called winning or losing only when the whole interval is above or below zero.

ITM (reached the paid places) is counted only where the files say it: tournaments without bounties, and satellites (a ticket is ITM). A bounty summary gives one total for place and knockouts, so bounty money counts in profit and ROI but not in ITM. Top 10 % / 15 % of the field are plain facts: your place over the number of players. A late registration flatters the place, so the late-reg table compares ROI.
help.backup.title: Backup and export
help.backup.body:
Settings → Backup: "Make a backup" saves the whole database into Downloads with the date. "Restore from a backup" checks the file first, keeps the current database next to itself, then replaces it; an older backup is upgraded.

Export CSV on the tournament list and in Hands saves what is shown into Downloads, for Excel. "Copy the result" and "Copy the hand" give plain text. A provisional prize is marked everywhere.
help.problems.title: Problems
help.problems.body:
• macOS will not open the app: System Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway" (the app is not signed).
  • Windows SmartScreen: "More info" → "Run anyway".
  • Where is my data? macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/PokerTracker; Windows: %APPDATA%\PokerTracker. Back it up from Settings.
  • A tournament says the summary is missing: download the summary from PokerCraft again; for a Day 2 GG sometimes offers it only later.
  • Numbers changed after an update: a definition or a fix changed; the changelog says which.
help.glossary.title: Glossary
help.glossary.body: <dl><dt>All-in EV</dt><dd>What an all-in is worth with your equity when the money went in; luck = actual result − EV.</dd><dt>Bounty / KO</dt><dd>Money for knocking a player out.</dd><dt>Flight / Day 2</dt><dd>Day-1 tournaments of a multi-day event; the stacks that go through meet on Day 2.</dd><dt>Late reg / re-entry</dt><dd>Joining after the start / buying in again after busting.</dd><dt>Limp</dt><dd>Calling the big blind first in.</dd><dt>Leak</dt><dd>A spot that costs you money beyond chance.</dd><dt>n</dt><dd>How many chances a rate rests on.</dd><dt>q</dt><dd>The chance a finding is a false alarm after the correction for every spot.</dd><dt>Showdown</dt><dd>Cards shown at the end of a hand.</dd><dt>Spot</dt><dd>A recurring situation, e.g. defending the big blind against an open.</dd><dt>Squeeze</dt><dd>A re-raise after a raise and a call.</dd></dl>
